key_insight: The paper reframes LLM evaluation from isolated tasks to a 14-domain, 91-subskill capability taxonomy that better organizes what models can actually do.
clinical_relevance: For clinical NLP, this can help researchers and developers spot coverage gaps, compare evaluations more consistently, and design more targeted model assessments.
method: Defined a multi-layer capability taxonomy using human cognitive science, not LLM architecture.
Grouped capabilities into Primitive, Constructed, and Integrative layers with 14 domains and 91 subskills.
Mapped 15,934 LLM-focused papers from ACL, AAAI, ICML, and NeurIPS (2023–2025) using multi-model annotation, consensus, and arbitration.
evidence_signal: Across 15,934 papers, attention concentrated on Language-Semantic Competence (22.3%), Reasoning (21.3%), Planning and Decision-Making (13.5%), and Perception (12.3%), while six domains appeared in fewer than 2% of papers.
watch_item: Because the taxonomy is built from human cognitive constructs and paper-level annotation, its usefulness may depend on how consistently different reviewers map tasks to capabilities.
paper_title: From Isolated Tasks to Structured Capabilities: A Multilayer Taxonomy for Large Language Models
